consulted_citations.field: 包 entry; pronunciation line and attributed received-form analysis
consulted_citations.text: The printed 包 headword gives bāo. Zhou Baohong calls 包 a 会意字, reading 勹 as wrapping, 巳 as an unborn child, and their combination as conveying 胞衣. He presents this as his account of the received form, not an independently verified origin. The entry also proposes that 包 should have existed in Western Zhou based on its use in the Shijing, while stating that it is not found in Shang or Western Zhou writing in his account. This is an attributed dating proposal, not an independently verified artifact attestation.

consulted_citations.text: The distinct 勹 headword gives modern Mandarin bāo and the historical-category notation 帮纽、幽部；帮纽、肴韵、布交切. This is the component character’s own printed reading, not a reading inferred from 包.
